 © 2026 Yahoo. All rights reserved. Henry Pollock starts for England at number eight in their Nations Championship clash against Japan, fresh from an electrifying two-try cameo against Australia.
 Head coach Steve Borthwick has rewarded the Northampton Saints standout with his second career Test start, offering him the opportunity to prove he's ready for a a permanent role in the starting XV.
 Advertisement Advertisement Advertisement Pollock's promotion comes as part of a sweeping overhaul by Borthwick, who has made 10 changes to the side that dispatched the Wallabies 45-22. Last weekend, Pollock showcased his remarkable versatility by stepping in out of position on the wing to replace the injured Immanuel Feyi-Waboso, crossing the whitewash twice in a statement performance. Against Japan, he returns to his natural habitat at the base of the scrum, allowing Ben Earl to shift across to openside flanker in a reshaped forward pack.

 As England continues to build towards the 2027 Six Nations , a commanding performance on Saturday could secure his status as a cornerstone of the English back row.
 To get the latest rugby news from WalesOnline in your search results, click here to add WalesOnline as a preferred source on Google 
 Advertisement Advertisement Advertisement Pollock's rise over the last two years has been extraordinary. After breaking into Northampton Saints' first team, he has become a Lions tourist, established himself in Steve Borthwick's England squad and emerged as one of world rugby's hottest properties.
 But the player dubbed 'King Henry the Eighth' by some fans and commentators, has already twice gone beyond the Rugby Football Union's own player welfare limits.
 Current player welfare guidelines recommending a maximum of 30 match involvements across a campaign. The 21-year-old went above that figure during BOTH of the last two campaigns, leading to fears about how England's brightest young star is being managed.
 Advertisement Advertisement Advertisement The limits were introduced by the RFU and its professional game partners as part of a drive to reduce burnout and protect players from long-term injuries. And Team England Rugby - the body which represents England's international players - admitted to The Telegraph in July that Pollock's workload was "a concern". England closely monitor every international through a specialist Player Load Management Group, with exemptions required whenever a player exceeds the recommended threshold.
 Henry Pollock of England during a training session at Pennyhill Park

 Advertisement Advertisement Advertisement The RFU acknowledges balancing club and international commitments remains a significant challenge and that's certainly the case where Pollock is concerned, given how integral he has become to Northampton Saints' PREM hopes.
 Northampton director of rugby Phil Dowson has previously argued that clubs should not shoulder all the responsibility for protecting leading players.
 "There has to be a negotiation and a relationship and a balance as to how many minutes they play and how many games they play," he said. "If Henry Pollock goes over his limit, is it entirely my responsibility to rest him going forward?
 Advertisement Advertisement Advertisement "There has to be talk around what is best for Henry. We've got to think about the next eight years of his career, not just the next eight months."
 Pollock, who despite only starting one of his 14 games for England before today has scored eight tries, will be making his 10th appearance of the season so far when he takes on the Brave Blossoms at Twickenham.
 Keeping him under that 30 game limit may well prove tricky yet again.
